components.text: The decisive demand is whether asserted unification establishes comparative explanatory superiority; the reply requires precedent, simplicity, and total-evidence likelihood.
Whether one fundamental mind actually yields superior comparative economy and total explanatory likelihood.
The decisive irreducibility demand is contacted by claiming that physical model-building computation inevitably produces differentiated qualitative experience.
Whether subjective qualitative experience can arise from physical computational model-building rather than fundamental mind.
The reply contacts the mind-first inference by comparing observed evolved brain dependence with the broader range of minds allegedly available under theism.
Whether mind is irreducible and physical reality is consequently derivative from mind.
The decisive resemblance inference is contacted by attributing cosmic-web and neural-network similarities to deterministic thermodynamic organization.
Whether cortical–cosmic-web resemblance preferentially supports a mind-like cosmic foundation.
The personal-ground demand is contacted by proposing empirically provable overriding hypothetical imperatives as a naturalistic basis for moral facts.
Whether objective moral obligations require a transcendent personal source rather than an empirical naturalistic ground.
The origin challenge is contacted by replacing absolute nothing with unrestricted possibilities and arguing probabilistically for a godless multiverse.
The reply also contests the one-mind economy claim by describing an omniscient and omnipotent God as maximally specified.
Whether one fundamental mind is genuinely simpler and more probable than the available naturalistic foundations.
Whether unrestricted random possibility is a coherent and probabilistically adequate cosmological alternative.
The reply contacts the personal-ground inference through evidence that moral codes developed gradually rather than appearing under perfect divine governance.
Whether the personal character of objective obligations requires their grounding in a transcendent perfect person.
The reply contacts the demand for a natural foundation by positing a geometric field state or random potential rather than literal nothing.
It also challenges the pro economy claim by presenting the minimally described state as simpler than God.
Whether the proposed natural origin is literally nothing and therefore lacks any coherent basis for possible outcomes.
Whether a minimal natural primitive is simpler than the proposed fundamental divine mind.
The reply identifies that absence of constraints is negative and therefore cannot supply the positive causal principles required for universe generation.
The same objection reaches the unrestricted-possibility model because a possible output set alone supplies no generator or probability measure.
Whether absence of governing laws supplies a positive causal and probabilistic basis for universe generation.
Whether unrestricted possibilities alone justify random selection and the asserted outcome probabilities.
The reply identifies that computational distinctions and neural correlations do not supply the missing explanation of subjective phenomenal character.
It also answers embodiment evidence by distinguishing observed correlation from reduction and claiming idealism can predict physical appearances.
Whether computational modeling explains subjective phenomenal experience rather than only correlated functions and discriminations.
Whether observed dependence on brains is more expected under naturalism than idealism or theism.
The reply directly compares the rival foundations on simplicity and claimed prediction of the total observed naturalistic pattern.
It restates the simple bubble as a brute fact but does not supply the positive causal or probabilistic principles demanded by the objection.
The selected synthesis does not contact the demand to explain subjective experience rather than neural or computational correlation.
Whether a single divine mind is simpler and predicts the combined evidence better than a minimal naturalistic foundation.
Whether the simple bubble has positive generative structure rather than merely an absence of constraints.
Whether naturalism explains subjective experience rather than only its neural correlations.
The simplicity demand is contacted by distinguishing mereological or ontological simplicity from the many capacities of an unlimited divine mind.
Whether an unlimited perfect mind must be infinitely complex and therefore less simple than the naturalistic primitive.
Whether maximal knowledge and power constitute infinite specified complexity despite divine partlessness.
